Subject: Renewal + capacity proposal for Lumina — draft quote and SLA addendum

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, attached is an updated quote (redwood-dedicated-quote-v2.pdf) that reflects:
- Renewal term: 12 months (renewal start 2026-11-01)
- Reserved pool: 8x A100 GPUs (baseline) + option to reserve an additional 4x A100s for burst/throughput (seat-based billing)
- Throughput guidance: baseline pool supports ~450 requests/sec at median request size; burst pool available for sustained peaks up to +50% from baseline when enabled.

I've also attached a draft SLA addendum (proposed-sla-addendum.docx) that captures latency & uptime targets we discussed and an exception clause for expanded capacity during the first 90 days post-renewal. Key asks for you to review:
- 95th percentile latency target (p95) for standard models: 150ms; optional committed p95 120ms with a 30% additional premium and dedicated burst capacity guarantees.
- Uptime target: 99.9% for core service on Dedicated pools; credits template included.
- 90-day performance validation window where we run mutually agreed load tests and can adjust autoscale/burst parameters.

If this looks reasonable, we'll loop Legal and Procurement to get a DocuSign-ready package. Happy to set up a 30-min tech + procurement sync this week.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the docs. A couple of clarifying questions from the product & infra side:

1) Our strict requirement: p95 inference latency needs to be <= 120ms for our real-time scoring endpoint under our typical payload (token avg ~120). Can Redwood meet that consistently with the proposed new pool + burst? If not, what does it look like to get there (config, cost)?
2) During peak trading hours we have short bursts that can be 10-12x normal QPS for ~8-12 minutes. We need to understand how autoscale and burst reservations interact — will those bursts cause throttling or much higher latencies?

Procurement (cc'd) also wants to understand the remediation/credit structure if p95 or uptime targets aren't met once we move to a reserved model.

Can we do a joint runbook/load test before signing? We'll need the results documented in the SLA addendum.

Cheers,
Aisha Kaur
Head of Product, Lumina Analytics

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity proposal for Lumina — draft quote and SLA addendum

Hi Aisha — quick technical reply from infra/solutions:

Short answer: with the configuration we proposed we expect steady-state p95 ~120–160ms depending on model variant and sequence length. A few details:
- Baseline pool (8x A100, no burst): expected p95 ~160ms for your token profile at target concurrency (unless you reduce max tokens).
- Baseline + reserved 4x A100 burst pool (always-on reservation for Lumina): our benchmarks show p95 can move to ~120–130ms for requests routed to nodes with dedicated cache warmed and favorable kernel placement.
- For the 10–12x short spikes: the burst pool + autoscaling will absorb short spikes if configured with burst headroom. However, there is a tradeoff: if you need strict p95 <=120ms for the entire window at 10–12x QPS, you will need to provision additional reserved capacity (estimated +6–8 GPUs) or accept a higher premium for guaranteed burst capacity.

Recommendations:
1) Start with the proposed 8+4 configuration and add a one-time performance validation run (we'll provide a test harness). If p95 is not within the agreed target, we will run tuning (batch/kv cache, kernel config) and re-run the test.
2) Add a clause that allows Lumina to ramp reserved capacity within the first 30 days of renewal with prorated billing — this reduces risk for both sides.
3) If Lumina signs up for the committed p95=120ms option (30% premium), we will lock in an expanded reserved pool to guarantee that target for peak windows.

I'm adding expected throughput numbers and a quick action list to the SLA doc. Happy to walk through specifics on a call.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Team —

Taking Neha's guidance, I've updated the SLA addendum and attached the revised quote (redwood-dedicated-quote-v2.pdf) and the addendum with a proposed compromise on the latency/upline credits. Highlights:
- Core uptime: 99.9% (standard) for reserved pool; credits scale by severity band.
- p95 SLO: default 150ms; optional committed 120ms with +30% premium and expansion to +6 GPUs during peak windows.
- 90-day validation: Redwood will run a mutually agreed load test within 14 days of renewal; if SLOs are not met, Redwood will implement tuning and/or transient capacity increases at no additional charge for the validation window.
- Prorated ramp clause: Lumina may request to increase reserved GPUs within the first 30 days; billing prorated and recorded in renewal invoice.

Next steps: please review the redlines in sla-addendum-redlines-lumina.docx and confirm procurement's priorities. If procurement agrees, we'll push to DocuSign and schedule the validation run (we can do it the week after signing).

Thanks —
Priyom

Priyom / Neha —

Procurement has reviewed the SLA addendum and submitted redlines (attached: sla-addendum-redlines-lumina.docx). The key requests:
1) Uptime target: change to 99.95% for core Dedicated pool or provide a larger credit ladder for misses.
2) Cap on credits: remove unilateral caps that prevent full remediation — we need clearer recovery commitments (we can negotiate hard caps but they must be meaningful).
3) Validation window: we require a 90-day operational acceptance period with two scheduled load tests and documented results.
4) Performance remedy: if p95 > 150ms after tuning during validation, Redwood must offer a 60-day trial expanded capacity at no charge or a service credit equal to 25% of the monthly host fee for the month following failure.

We attached redlines; please confirm Redwood's legal/commercial stance so procurement can prepare a PO and get finance sign-off.

Regards,
Lumina Procurement
procurement@lumina-analytics.com

Aisha / Procurement —

Appreciate the clear redlines. We discussed internally (sales + solutions + CS + legal) and can accept the following compromise to get you to signature quickly:

1) Uptime: agree to 99.95% for the core Dedicated pool for the renewal term, with the credit ladder moved earlier (larger credits for outages beyond the first hour).
2) Latency SLO: we will keep default p95=150ms in the base addendum but commit to the two-step plan you requested:
   - Validation: two scheduled load tests during the 90-day acceptance period (dates to be mutually agreed) and documented runbooks.
   - Remedy: if, after tuning, p95 remains >150ms, Redwood will provide either (a) a 60-day expanded reserved pool sized to target p95<=150ms at no additional charge or (b) a service credit equal to 25% of one month’s Dedicated fee (Lumina chooses).
3) Committed 120ms option remains available as an add-on (30% premium + explicit reserved capacity + contractual burst guarantees).
4) Prorated ramp clause: confirmed — Lumina can request reserved GPU increases in the first 30 days; billing prorated.

If this is acceptable, we'll incorporate the agreed wording into the addendum, push the package to DocuSign (link below), and target signature by Oct 18 so we can schedule the validation run for the week of Oct 20.
